question: What's the Difference Between a Post's Excerpt and Its Content?
metaDescription: Content is the full post; the excerpt is a short summary used in archive listings, RSS feeds and search results when the full content isn't shown.
shortAnswer: The content is the full post itself. The excerpt is a short, separate summary — either manually written in its own editor field, or automatically generated by truncating the content if left blank — used specifically in places where showing the entire post would be inappropriate: archive listings, RSS feeds, and sometimes search result snippets, all of which benefit from a concise preview rather than the full text.

image.alt: A short manually written excerpt summarizing a post, used in archive listings instead of showing the full content

bodyHtml:
How the Excerpt Field Works

The Excerpt field (available in the post editor's sidebar, sometimes needing to be enabled via editor options) lets you write a short, purpose-built summary distinct from the opening lines of the actual content. If left empty, WordPress automatically generates one by truncating the post content to a default word count, which works but often cuts off mid-sentence or misses the actual key point a manually crafted summary could capture.

Why a Manual Excerpt Is Usually Better

  • An automatically truncated excerpt simply cuts the content at a word count, regardless of whether that produces a coherent, compelling summary — it often reads awkwardly compared to something purpose-written.
  • A manually written excerpt can be crafted specifically to entice a reader to click through from an archive listing, functioning almost like a mini call-to-action rather than just a content preview.
  • Some SEO plugins use the excerpt (or a separate meta description field) differently for search engine snippets, so it's worth understanding which field a specific plugin actually pulls from for that purpose.
  • RSS feed readers typically show the excerpt rather than full content by default in many feed configurations, making it worth treating as genuinely reader-facing content, not an afterthought.

Using Excerpts Well

  1. Write a manual excerpt for important content, rather than relying on automatic truncation.
  2. Keep it genuinely summarizing the piece, written to work well as a standalone preview.
  3. Check which specific field an SEO plugin uses for search snippets, since it may be a separate meta description rather than the excerpt itself.

Need help optimizing archive and search snippet display? See WordPress bug fix.
